chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام sent to Zurarah that he should inform al-Hakam ibn 'Uyaybah that the successors of Muhammad, upon him and upon them be peace, are muhaddathun.

key_terms.أَوْصِيَاءَ: the designated successors entrusted with authority after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْحَكَمَ بْنَ عُتَيْبَةَ: the individual to whom this theological point was to be conveyed
key_terms.مُحَدَّثُونَ: those who are spoken to or inspired through divine communication without being prophets
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ: the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean when it says the successors of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم are مُحَدَّثُونَ?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the awsiya' of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم possess the rank of being muhaddathun, meaning recipients of divine communication not in the form of prophethood. It highlights a distinctive theological status of the Imams in Shia doctrine and affirms their special access to divinely bestowed knowledge.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws sent Zurara that he should let Al-Hakam Bin Uteyba (The famous philosopher Al-Kindy) know that the successorsasws of Muhammadsaww, upon himsaww and upon themasws be the greetings, are Muhaddisoun (to whom the Angels discuss)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following.

“Abu Ja‘far (a.s.) sent (message) to Zurara to inform al-Hakam ibn ‘Utayba that the executors of the will of Muhammad (s.a.) (are Muhaddathun) hear from the angels.” al-Hakam ibn ’Utaybah (al-Kindi al-Kufi [50/670 - 115/ 733], one of the tab‘un [those who knew the companions of the Holy Prophet and famous narrators of hadith)
